items.title: Two Waves, One Stage Apart: Warp-Pipelining Triton GEMMs on AMD Instinct
items.summary: A tiled general matrix multiplication (GEMM) computes on one pair of operand tiles while preparing the next. On a compute-bound shape, keeping the matrix units busy depends on how well those activities overlap. A common failure mode is that resident waves reach synchronization points in phase: both prepare data or wait, and neither has matrix work ready to issue. Extra buffering creates room for future tiles, but does not by itself establish the execution timing needed to hide that preparation.

items.summary: Interactive world models keep the KV of past chunks as retrieval memory so that revisited places stay consistent. The first is capacity: the KV of Matrix-Game 2.0 exhausts host memory after 45 seconds of video in bf16 and after 2.8 minutes in int4. The second is the model's positional horizon of 4.3 minutes.
